payload.explanation: Observed: the slip monitor (reference = line_green position in tcp frame captured at the grasped_line_green phase, offset z 0.0760 m) fired during the descent move_grasp_center_to_pose (skill_start 1792970080216882000, target grasp-centre z 0.0524). object_poses and frames evidence: until ~1792970081.65e9 ns the part tracked the tcp exactly (tcp z 0.1883 / part z 0.1122, offset 0.0761). From ~1792970082.55e9 the part stopped descending at world z ~0.074 and rotated: line_green quaternion x went from 0.0003 to -0.22 (~25 deg tilt about the world x axis), while the tcp kept descending from 0.165 to 0.128 m. The tcp-to-part offset fell to ~0.060 m at the fire and ~0.054 m when the move settled. Total slip ~0.022 m, beyond the 0.02 m raw_spec.tolerances.grasp_slip_tolerance_m. All of this happened while line_green was still held: release_skill had not yet started, its skill_start came at 1792970087026829000. Why a departure: the in-hand slippage invariant forbids the part moving relative to the gripper before release; it did. Mechanism (my interpretation): the carried line_green struck the base1 fixture, or the seated u_brown/u_orange walls, about 0.02 m above its seat. It jammed, tilted ~25 deg, and the fingers slid down it as the arm completed its commanded descent. That is part-on-part collision during insertion, not spontaneous slip. Evidence cannot settle which surface it struck. Seating against line_green_placement is evaluated separately at end_step.

payload.explanation: Context: after place_line_green closed with claimed_outcome failure, the executor ran an unannounced recovery. There was no begin_step, so this activity sits outside any declared step and is attributed here to the last step, place_line_green; it is not on the expected process. It ran two re-pick and re-place cycles of line_green (grasp_skill at 1792970136.8e9 and 1792970249.5e9). Observed: during the second cycle's lift (skill_start 1792970262189696000, height 0.2 m), object_poses show u_brown, which is seated, inactive, and not acted on by this lift, rising with line_green. Its z went 0.0438 -> 0.0532 -> 0.0605 m and qx went from -0.70 to -0.24 (~70 deg roll) while line_green rose from 0.076 to 0.208 m. u_brown then fell to rest at (0.40219, -0.18605, 0.05038) with orientation (0, 0, -0.106, 0.994). That is ~0.034 m from its rest pose and rotated ~90 deg from its seated orientation. The authored stationarity monitor fired at 0.0221 m against the 0.02 m raw_spec.tolerances.disturbance_tolerance_m. Why a departure: the undisturbed-objects invariant requires u_brown to stay where it last came to rest until a step acts on it; no step acted on it here. Mechanism (my interpretation): line_green was re-grasped while still cocked ~21 deg and wedged against u_brown's wall. Lifting it straight up hooked or friction-dragged u_brown out of the base1 slot. It was then released and tipped over beside the fixture. This is a carried-part-on-part disturbance, the ACM-permitted channel. u_brown is now unseated, and its earlier milestone result no longer reflects its state.

payload.explanation: Context: this is the third line_green insertion attempt in the executor's unannounced recovery after place_line_green failed. There was no begin_step, so it is attributed to the last declared step; it is not on the expected process. u_brown was lying displaced in or near line_green's slot after the previous finding. Observed in object_poses: during move_grasp_center_to_pose (solve_ik_first, skill_start 1792970284610446000 to skill_end 1792970296097860000, target grasp-centre z 0.0524), line_green descended to z ~0.082. It then tilted to qx 0.22 and then 0.38 (~45 deg) as the arm kept driving. Over the same ~5 s, u_brown was levered up and rolled: z 0.050 -> 0.065, qx 0 -> 0.58, y -0.186 -> -0.160. u_orange was pushed +0.030 m in world y off its seat, and base1 itself slid +0.030 m in y. The base1 monitor fired at 0.0247 m, and base1 has stayed at the displaced pose since. release_skill then left line_green cocked at z 0.091. Why a departure: base1 is the fixture and must stay undisturbed. u_orange was seated, inactive and not acted on by this re-place. Both exceed the 0.02 m raw_spec.tolerances.disturbance_tolerance_m. Mechanism (my interpretation): the carried line_green was driven down onto u_brown, which now obstructed the slot. Because the motion was position-controlled to the seat pose, the jam was resolved by shoving the whole stack. u_brown was wedged sideways, and base1 and the seated u_orange were pushed ~3 cm in +y. This is carried-part-on-part collision through the ACM-permitted channel. No bystander from the other assembly moved.

payload.explanation:
This is the run's final end-state verdict: non_conformant. The executor aborted (run_ended status aborted) with violations still standing.

End-state, measured by me with query_snapshot after run_ended. The placement frames ride on base1, which itself ended displaced 0.0297 m (+y) from its run-start pose.
- u_brown: 0.043 m from u_brown_placement (tolerance 0.01 m) and rolled ~70 deg. It is not seated. It was seated correctly at its place_u_brown milestone (0.0022 m) but was later knocked out.
- u_orange: 0.0014 m from u_orange_placement and ~2.6 deg off. Within tolerance, because it was shoved together with base1 and stayed in its slot.
- line_green: 0.043 m from line_green_placement (tolerance 0.015 m) and tilted ~45 deg. Never seated.
- inverted_u_yellow: never attempted; still at its start pose.
- Bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2): unmoved throughout (<0.1 mm).

Timeline. Steps 1-8 checked clean against evidence: lifts 0.20/0.20/0.30 m, peak clamp efforts 61.8/75.4/16.7 against limits 100/200/170, no slip, no disturbance, and both U parts seated within tolerance at their milestones. Four findings were recorded under place_line_green:
- (1) In-hand slip of ~0.022 m: line_green jammed ~2 cm above its seat and tilted ~25 deg.
- (2) Misseat at end_step: 0.021 m high and 24.5 deg tilted. The executor itself claimed failure.
- (3) During the executor's unannounced recovery, which had no begin_step and is not on the expected process, lifting the cocked line_green dragged the seated u_brown out of its slot.
- (4) A third forced insertion onto the obstructed slot shoved base1 and u_orange ~3 cm.
None of these was corrected: u_brown and line_green remain misseated and base1 remains displaced.

Not evaluable as stated: effects.object_tcp_offset_m. The absolute tcp-to-object-frame offset (~0.076-0.091 m) reflects frame-origin geometry; in-hand stability was assessed instead as the change in that offset against grasp_slip_tolerance_m. Grip width relied on the executor's reported width, since no independent width channel was available.

Scene: looks at run start and run end show no unlisted object or foreign presence, so no observation was recorded. Mid-run scene coverage was limited to step-boundary checks and pose monitors.
